column5: F: A project, and an empty tab? | M: The drawings are untracked files.
column6: F: A project with two stages, and nothing in its BIM Document tab? | M: Right. Its drawings are just files that nobody tracks.

column5: F: What links a drawing to an invoice? | M: One chain.
column6: F: So what links a drawing to an invoice? | M: A single chain. The sheet, the BIM Document, the project task, and the invoice.

column5: F: And after? | M: Two of three sheets issued.
column6: F: And the same project, after? | M: Now it has a register. Two of three plan sheets are issued, and the phase shows three of four.

column5: F: Where does it get its stages? | M: From the project type.
column6: F: Where does it get its stages? | M: From the project type. This type is Consulting. Running it copies its three phases and two tasks into the project.

column5: F: So how many phases now? | M: Five.
column6: F: So how many phases does the project have now? | M: Five. Its own two, plus the three from the type.

column5: F: And the drawings? | M: Each sheet is a row under a task.
column6: F: And the drawings? Where do they go? | M: Each sheet becomes a row under a task, with a number, a title, a discipline and a file kind.

column5: F: You type them in? | M: Here, yes.
column6: F: So you type them in? | M: I will type this sheet. The others are entered the same way. | F: What about the project and the phase? | M: They come from the task the sheet is entered under.

column5: F: How many on this task? | M: Three.
column6: F: How many sheets on this task? | M: Three. The register counts three rows, and three deliverables. | F: Is that counted by the system, or by you? | M: By the system. The BIM progress action reads the register and reports it.

column5: F: How does the file get in? | M: The attachment button.
column6: F: And the drawing itself? | M: It goes on the row through the attachment button. A small test drawing, seventy-nine bytes. Its fingerprint begins c, eight, two, five, four, zero.

column5: F: Can I open it from here? | M: In the Modeller, yes.
column6: F: Can I open it from here? | M: Open in Modeller. And the Modeller logs the same fingerprint it was handed, beginning c, eight, two, five, four, zero.

column5: F: Who says it is ready? | M: The action bar: review, then construction.
column6: F: Who says a sheet is ready? | M: The document action bar. A draft goes to review first, then out for construction. | F: Is that written down? | M: Each step is a recorded transition, and the bar only offers the legal ones.

column5: F: And a revision? | M: Revision one becomes superseded.
column6: F: And when the drawing changes? | M: A revision is a new row. Issue revision two for construction, and revision one becomes superseded, linked to the new row.

column5: F: What about hours? | M: Booked on the task.
column6: F: What about the hours? | M: They are booked on the same task. Three time lines, seven hours in total.

column4: b8.task.issued, b8.task.total, b8.task.earned, b8.task.budget, b8.phase.issued, b8.phase.total, b8.phase.earned, b8.phase.budget
column5: F: Who types the progress? | M: Nobody. It is computed.
column6: F: And the progress? Who types that? | M: Nobody. It is computed. On this task, one sheet of three is issued, with eight hours earned of twenty-four. | F: And the phase? | M: Two of four, twenty-two hours earned of thirty-eight.

column5: F: And the money? | M: Tick the phase, Generate Order.
column6: F: And when does it turn into money? | M: Tick the phase complete. This stage is priced: eight hours at fifty. | F: And then? | M: Run its Generate Order. It makes an order with one line, four hundred.

column5: F: And the invoice? | M: Complete the order, and it follows.
column6: F: And the invoice? | M: Complete the order, and the invoice follows. | F: Can I reach it from the order? | M: Yes, Zoom Across takes you to it. | F: With the same amounts? | M: Line for line. Eight at fifty, four hundred.

column5: F: Does the count follow? | M: Two to three.
column6: F: Does the sheet count follow? | M: Issue one more sheet, and the issued count moves one link, from two to three.

column5: F: Is this a real project? | M: No. Test data.
column6: F: Is this a real project? | M: No. A test server, with a synthetic Duplex sheet set.
